critique.good: Every column gets exactly its one-line width, so headers are 6/6 on one line, teacher names (רונית לוי, אבי שפירא, דוד מזרחי) and room labels (אולם ספורט, מעבדה 1) stay whole, no mid-word splits, and the notes column (256px of text) is as wide as it can be without breaking any other cell. The day band on the right reads as a clear anchor and the day labels are not competing with anything.
critique.problems: Notes still forces 3 lines in four rows, so the vertical rhythm is lumpy (36/83/83/60/60/83/60/83) and the table is 547px tall. The lesson columns are pinned to the pixel (מורה 89, חדר 97) with zero breathing room, while הערות occupies 38% of the table; the eye reads a tight identity block next to a wide prose block.
critique.cause: Columns 2–5 were given their exact one-line minimums (110/84/89/97) which leaves only 277px for הערות; any note longer than ~34 characters per line wraps to a third line.

critique.good: The most comfortable table to look at cell by cell: generous gutters, nothing cramped, teacher and room clearly separated from subject, notes still legible and never mid-word broken.
critique.problems: At 720×663 it is 116px taller than r0A for exactly the same information; rows alternate 83/106 and the rhythm feels bloated. Meanwhile שעה (120 vs 110 needed), מקצוע (95 vs 84), מורה (100 vs 89) and חדר (114 vs 97) all carry visible slack, so the notes column looks starved beside fat neighbours.
critique.cause: Over-allocation to the first five columns (8–17px each of unused width) starves הערות down to 199px of text, pushing most notes to 3–4 lines and inflating every row.

critique.good: The shortest and most even table: 477px, most rows a single 60px height, notes at 312px of text reads in a calm 2–3 lines, and the day blocks stay crisp.
critique.problems: The identity columns are damaged. Teacher names split across two lines (רונית / לוי, אבי / שפירא, שרה / כהן, דוד / מזרחי, מיכל / אדרי), the venue splits אולם / ספורט, and worst, מעבדה 1 breaks so the number is orphaned on its own line under its label. Scanning מורה or חדר down the column becomes stop-and-start.
critique.cause: מורה and חדר were set to their longest unbreakable word (42+21=63 and 46+21=67) instead of their one-line widths (89 and 97), so every two-word name or label wraps and numbers detach from their labels.

critique.good: Compact 500px table with an even rhythm. Notes at 294px (273px text) keeps five of seven notes blocks to two lines, so only the two genuinely long notes (פיזיקה, חינוך גופני) run to three lines — the minimum possible at 720px. Day, time, subject and teacher all sit on one line, and חדר at 80px is just wide enough to keep 'מעבדה 1' intact.
critique.problems: In the last row the room 'אולם ספורט' breaks into two lines — a lone wrapped cell in an otherwise single-line room column, and the room numbers live in a narrow 59px lane. Because that row is already three lines tall from its notes, the wrap costs no height, so it is a minor blemish rather than a structural fault.
critique.cause: col5 = 80px yields 59px of text, 17px short of the 76px needed for 'אולם ספורט'; the width was tuned to the shorter 'מעבדה 1' rather than to the longest room label.

critique.good: חדר at 97px (76px text) fits 'אולם ספורט' on one line, so every room cell is a clean single line and the room column reads as a calm, uniform strip.
critique.problems: Funding that 17px from the notes column (294→277, text 273→256) pushes two more notes blocks (the first two rows) from two to three lines, so the table grows to 547px and the row rhythm becomes more uneven (83,83,60…). Meanwhile the room column now carries 17px of dead space around the three-digit numbers in six of seven rows: width taken from the text-heavy column and given to the emptiest one.
critique.cause: The 17px shift from col6 to col5 crosses the notes line-break threshold (256 < the ~265–273px needed for two lines); the room column was widened for one exceptional cell. Note that with teacher kept one-line, all five non-notes columns already sum to 442px, so notes can never exceed 277px if חדר is to stay one-line — the two goals are mutually exclusive.

critique.good: The notes column at 300px (279px of content) keeps annotations to at most 3 lines, so row heights stay predictable. Room labels are intact on one line — "אולם ספורט" and "מעבדה 1" both read cleanly — and all six column headers sit on a single line, so the header band is calm and the day/time anchors line up neatly down the right edge.
critique.problems: The teacher column is the failure point: every single name breaks into two stacked fragments (רונית/לוי, אבי/שפירא, שרה/כהן, דוד/מזרחי, יעל/ברק, מיכל/אדרי, עומר/פרץ). Since מורה is part of the lesson's identity, the reader cannot compare teachers down the column at a glance; the eye keeps re-assembling two-line blobs. Meanwhile the room column, whose content is mostly a three-digit number, carries visible slack — so the allocation is inverted relative to information value: the column with the most semantic weight is starved while the sparsest numeric column is comfortable. The result is a grid where every lesson row looks vertically ragged in one column and airy in another.
critique.cause: מורה = 66px leaves only 45px of content against a 68px one-line width, so all names must wrap. חדר = 97px gives exactly the 76px needed for "אולם ספורט", which is why the room column is safe but the teacher column is not.

critique.good: Teacher names now sit on one line (מורה = 89px gives the full 68px), so the lesson identity reads as a single unit and the column scans vertically. מקצוע, שעה and יום are unchanged and intact, headers are all single-line, and — importantly — total row heights are identical to r2A (max 3 lines), because the room wrap only happens in rows already made tall by their notes. So the fix cost nothing in table height.
critique.problems: The room column is now the cramped one: "אולם ספורט" splits into אולם / ספורט and "מעבדה 1" into מעבדה / 1, while bare numbers like 204, 112, 305 sit alone on a line. The room column therefore looks inconsistent — sometimes one line, sometimes two — and in the last row the two-line room label looks stranded beside a three-line note. The subject column is also at exactly zero slack, which is risky.
critique.cause: חדר = 70px leaves 49px of content, well under the 76px one-line width of "אולם ספורט", so that cell must wrap; מקצוע = 84px gives exactly the 63px of "מתמטיקה" with no safety margin.

understanding.purpose: A Hebrew RTL class timetable for grade י'2, semester א', used to find when a lesson occurs, who teaches it, where it meets, and any special instructions.
understanding.reading: Readers scan from the right: first the merged day block, then the time, then subject/teacher/room as the lesson identity, and finally the notes as exceptions or instructions. Day rowspans group consecutive lessons, so those blocks must remain visually coherent.
groups: יום + שעה — temporal anchors read first and define each rowspan block
מקצוע + מורה + חדר — the lesson's identity and location, compared across rows
הערות — secondary free-text annotations that can absorb wrapping
keep_intact: teacher names at least at word level
room numbers and room labels at word level
may_wrap: הערות prose, which is long and naturally multi-line
multi-word room labels such as אולם ספורט at spaces
teacher full names at spaces only in a notes-priority design

bad.why: The notes column is starved at 277px, forcing extra prose wraps and making the table 547px tall; meanwhile the room column gets 97px for mostly 3-digit codes. Width is misallocated and the table loses its compact rhythm.
Same fault as r1B: identical widths, 547px height, notes over-wrapped at 277px while the room column is over-wide. The extra height buys no useful room-label improvement.

The teacher column is only 66px, so every teacher name breaks into two lines, while the room column is widened to 97px for short codes. This inverts the natural priority of names versus room numbers and leaves the row-scanning key field fragmented.

final.rationale: This is a weekly schedule, so day and time must stay terse while teacher and room remain scannable identifiers; the notes column is the only prose and should absorb the leftover width. r1A and r3C do that: 62/110/84/89 are enough for day, time, subject and full teacher names, 80–84 keeps 'מעבדה 1' on one line, and 290–294 still holds notes to three lines with a 500px table. r1B/r3A invert the priority by over-widening room and starving notes, adding 47px of height for no gain in the short room codes. The day column can stay at 62px because its longest label and header fit exactly, and the merged day groups still read clearly.

general: Allocate width by content type: keep names and short identifiers on one line; let prose wrap.
Equal column widths are usually wrong; numeric/time columns can be tight while prose columns need width.
A column wider than its line-count threshold is wasted width; stop when extra pixels no longer reduce wrapping.
Row-header columns, especially merged group labels, need enough width to stay intact and visually distinct.
specific: Time strings need about 110px; teacher names need about 89px; room labels need 80–84px; notes are best around 290–294px here.
The day column at 62px exactly fits the longest day label and header; wider is unnecessary.
'אולם ספורט' is the only room value that wants 97px; keeping it on one line is not worth reducing notes to 277px.
Below roughly 285px the notes column starts adding rows, so the table grows from 500px to 547px.

final.tradeoffs: r0C is the compact option at 477px and gives notes 333px, but it splits every teacher name and 'מעבדה 1' across two lines; some designers may accept that for the shorter table. r2B/r3B trade a little notes width for room width and tolerate two-line room labels. Keeping 'אולם ספורט' on one line would require 97px for room, which pushes notes to 277px and makes the table noticeably taller.
final.uncertain: Whether full teacher names must remain on one line, and whether the compact r0C is preferable despite fragmented names. The exact notes-width threshold around 285–290px may vary slightly with font rendering, and reasonable designers could disagree on whether 'אולם ספורט' should be kept unbroken at the cost of notes width.

B.why: Balanced and readable: times stay on one line and key columns hold; notes are slightly tighter than in D, with more wrapping.

C.why: Notes are crushed into a narrow strip, one or two words per line, making the table extremely tall while other columns sit mostly empty.

D.why: Best proportion: times, subjects, teachers and rooms remain scannable, while notes get enough width for readable multi-line blocks; rows have an even rhythm.

E.why: Teacher names and room labels break across lines in most rows, making the schedule busy and harder to scan; notes are cramped.

F.why: Times and notes are usable, but room identifiers such as מעבדה 1 split across lines and the allocation is less clean than D/B.

reviews.unsure: Exact column widths are hard to measure from screenshots; B and D are close, and some room/teacher wraps are borderline.
